# University of Chicago
The University of Chicago was re-established in 1890 with significant funding from John D. Rockefeller and constructed its Hyde Park campus under a master plan inspired by Oxford's collegiate Gothic style. It opened in 1892 under President William Rainey Harper, who emphasized faculty research and a rigorous academic curriculum divided between an Academic College and University College. The university fostered early programs in theology, athletics, and extension education while evolving through financial austerity and expansions under successive presidents.
Notably, the university contributed to pivotal scientific developments including the Manhattan Project with faculty such as Enrico Fermi engineering the first self-sustaining nuclear reaction. Its social sciences gave rise to the Chicago schools of economics and sociology. The campus now spans 217 acres in Hyde Park, featuring historic architecture and modern facilities like the Mansueto Library. The university operates multiple satellite campuses globally, including in Hong Kong, London, Paris, Beijing, and New Delhi.
Academically, the University of Chicago is highly selective with an acceptance rate below 5% and offers a liberal arts core curriculum emphasizing the Socratic method. It comprises a College of Arts and Sciences, four graduate divisions, and seven professional schools such as the Booth School of Business and Pritzker School of Medicine. It maintains a strong research profile with $424 million in R&D spending (2018), managing national labs including Argonne and Fermilab.
Student life includes over 400 student organizations, a house system for undergraduates, and traditions like the annual Scavenger Hunt. The university fields NCAA Division III athletic teams called the Maroons and reinstated football in 1969. Its diverse alumni network includes 101 Nobel laureates and leaders across politics, science, and the arts, including former President Barack Obama.
Governed by a 55-member board of trustees and led by President Paul Alivisatos since 2021, the University of Chicago had a $10 billion endowment in 2024 but is managing financial deficits with budget cuts planned. Its main campus is served by multiple transit options, maintains one of the largest private police forces in the U.S., and has expanded its facilities and global presence while upholding a reputation as a prestigious research university.
